previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of systolic heart failure (EF 20%), ischemic cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and obesity, was readmitted five days after a prior discharge for worsening shortness of breath, chest heaviness, and leg swelling. He had gained 2 pounds and reported persistent symptoms despite medication adherence. Evaluation revealed acute on chronic systolic heart failure exacerbation with elevated BNP, pulmonary edema on imaging, and volume overload. He was treated with IV diuresis and transitioned back to oral torsemide 140 mg daily. A Persantine MIBI stress test showed a new severe fixed inferior wall defect and moderate reversible inferolateral defect, with an ejection fraction of 28%. His symptoms improved, weight decreased to 130.4 kg, and he was discharged home with service, follow-up plans for cardiology evaluation of ischemia, medication blister packs for adherence support, and instructions to monitor weight and use nitroglycerin as needed.
